dedupe_keys.name: psml a multi scale time series dataset for machine learning in decarbonized energy grids

description: PSML is an open multi-scale time-series data set built to support machine learning for reliable operation of grids with high renewable and electrified-transport shares. It was published in 2021 by Xiangtian Zheng, Nan Xu, Dongqi Wu, Loc Trinh, Tong Huang, S. Sivaranjani, Yan Liu and Le Xie, with code in the Texas A&M engineering research GitHub organisation. The data were generated by a transmission-plus-distribution co-simulation that captures interactions and uncertainty in grid dynamics. Contents include minute-level load, wind, solar and weather data for 2018 to 2020 in zones of US system operators such as CAISO, and millisecond-level voltage and current measurements for disturbance events. The release includes machine learning baselines for three tasks: detecting, classifying and locating dynamic disturbances; hierarchical forecasting of load and renewables under uncertainty and extreme events; and generating synthetic measurement series that respect physical laws. Coverage is US operator zones with simulated test grids. Files are CSV in a ZIP of about 5.2 GB, downloadable from Zenodo (version 0.2, 2021) under CC BY 4.0 at no cost. Caveats: event data are simulated, and load and renewable values are normalised. Simulation uses are disturbance detection and forecasting benchmarks.
